hypothesis: The stability failure in experiment 1 was caused by doubling gait_phase_regularity weight to -2.0, which forced the policy to optimize for strict rhythmic cadence before it had mastered basic locomotion — creating self-defeating competing objectives at this curriculum stage. Reverting gait_phase_regularity_reward_weight to -1.0 removes that constraint. The limb_symmetry_velocity_weight change (0.1 → 0.5) was never fairly evaluated since the run was cut at 25%. By keeping that single change, this experiment cleanly isolates the velocity-symmetry effect: the policy should now have enough room to develop gait while being guided toward better left-right velocity synchronisation, addressing the "mirror-pose limp" risk (symmetry_pos_cost small but symmetry_vel_cost potentially elevated). Expected side-effect per domain rule #6: no major change to tracking reward since the gait_regularity competition pressure is removed.
expected_effects: fell_over_rate drops well below 1.0 by iteration 1000 (stability gate passes) — the primary success criterion for this run
gait_contact_cv_mean stabilises or improves from the 0.576 high reached in experiment 1, returning toward baseline ~0.33
symmetry_vel_cost_mean decreases relative to the original baseline (better velocity synchronisation between legs)
track_linear_velocity reward remains near its strong level (~1.18) since gait-regularity competition pressure is removed
symmetry_pos_cost_mean remains roughly unchanged (position symmetry weight untouched — this is the diagnostic check: if pos_cost also changes, something unexpected is happening)
